payload.name: PreserveExplicitHobbyOrigin
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states how, why, or through whom they started a hobby, interest, or preference, use this to extract and retain that origin alongside the current state.
content: During candidate extraction, if a statement explicitly gives the origin or cause of a hobby, interest, or preference, include that origin in the extracted memory content rather than only recording the current state.
When persisting, if the origin supplements an existing memory, use UPDATE or MERGE to add the missing detail; do not create a duplicate ADD that omits it.
Do not discard explicit causal or influential details such as another person's advice or introduction when those details answer how or why the preference began.

candidates.solves: When a speaker explicitly explains how they started or got into a hobby, interest, or preference, extraction often keeps only the resulting state and drops the causal origin. This skill requires preserving explicitly stated origins so future questions about how something began are answerable, across any hobby or interest topic.

payload.name: CaptureStatedPurposeBehindCreativeWork
payload.description: When a user explains the reason, purpose, or inspiration behind a creative work they made, extract a memory recording that stated purpose.
content: During candidate extraction, if a user explains what their creative work (e.g., drawing, writing, music) is for or why they made it, create a state or preference memory with the user as subject, the creative work as object, and the stated purpose as the value.
Treat the user's own explanation as authoritative unless contradicted elsewhere; do not infer additional purposes beyond what they state.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed failure is that the extraction stage produced no memory when a user explained the purpose behind a creative artifact (drawings) in a conversational reply. The abstract mechanism is that explanatory purpose statements following a compliment or direct question are often overlooked during candidate extraction. This skill applies to any future session where a user states why they created something or what it helps them achieve, ensuring the stated purpose is captured as a durable memory.

payload.name: Extract creative inspiration statements
payload.description: When a user explicitly states what inspired or influenced their creative work (script, book, movie, etc.), extract that fact into memory.
content: During candidate extraction, identify user statements that explicitly name an inspiration or influence for a creative project (e.g., 'sparked ideas for my next script', 'inspired by X').
Create a memory that links the creative project to the stated inspiration source, using a suitable memory type such as 'plan' or 'relationship' to preserve the fact.

candidates.solves: This addresses construction failures where explicit user statements about what inspired or influenced a creative project (e.g., a script, book, movie) are not extracted into memory, leaving later questions about the inspiration unanswered. The rule applies whenever a user directly names a source of inspiration for a creative work; it does not apply when inspiration must be inferred from implicit context.

payload.name: Extract user values from symbolic reminders
payload.description: When a user mentions an object, image, or keepsake that exists to remind them of a value or goal, extract that stated value as a durable profile/preference memory during construction.
content: During candidate extraction, if the user links a personal object or symbol to a value or aspiration (e.g., 'I have a painting to remind me to stay true'), create a profile memory for the stated value, not for the object.
Attribute the value to the user, never to a referenced third party or fictional character mentioned in the same sentence.
Record the memory as evidence-bound to the exact message and keep the object detail only as context, not as the memory's subject.

candidates.solves: The construction run produced no candidates for an explicit first-person statement in which a user disclosed a personal value through a symbolic reminder (e.g., a painting that reminds them to stay true and be a leader). The failure mechanism is under-extraction of value/aspiration statements when they are attached to physical objects. This skill generalizes to any future session where a user mentions a keepsake, symbol, or reminder that encodes their own value or goal, and it applies only to the user's self-disclosure, not to facts about characters or other people.

payload.name: Extract hobby-origin narratives
payload.description: When a user explains how they got into or started a hobby, interest, or activity, retrieve this skill to ensure the origin story is stored, not just the current preference.
content: During extraction, when a person describes the beginning of a hobby or interest (e.g., who introduced it, a gift, advice, or what inspired them), capture those origin facts as part of the memory candidate, not only the generic current preference.

Store the origin narrative as a durable event or preference memory linked to the person, including the initiator and any specific gift/advice/inspiration mentioned; do not collapse it into a single generic statement about enjoying the activity.

During CRUD, if later messages add or clarify how the person started the activity, update the existing memory with the missing origin details rather than leaving only the preference or current activity summary.

candidates.solves: Memory extraction can collapse 'how I started X' into a generic current preference, dropping the initiator, gift, or inspiration needed to answer origin questions. This skill enforces capturing the full origin narrative when a person describes beginning a hobby, and updating earlier memories when later messages add such details. It applies to future origin explanations, not to simple statements of current enjoyment.

payload.name: Extract-Origin-Event-From-Journey-Narrative
payload.description: When a user narrates how they started an activity or hobby, extract the origin event (who, what, when) as a separate memory candidate, not only a summary of the journey.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a personal origin story (e.g., "When I was [age], [person] signed me up for [activity]" or "I started [activity] because [reason]"), create a distinct `event` memory capturing the specific introducer, action, age/time, and activity, even when you also create a broader life-journey memory.
Do not omit the initiating detail just because the broader journey is already summarized; the origin fact is independently queryable (e.g., "How did X get into Y?").
Preserve the causal structure: who introduced the person and the specific enaction (e.g., signed up, bought first equipment, joined a team).

candidates.solves: The extractor compressed a life-journey narrative into one summary memory and lost the origin event, so the answer to 'how did X get into Y?' was missing. This is a general extraction failure pattern when a speaker narrates how they began an activity; the origin fact (introducer, action, time) must be extracted as a separate event memory. Applies to any future story-telling session about starting a hobby, sport, career, or skill.
